clue.text: Court official's room left in a mess

parts.note: a chamber is a room, especially a private or formal one

indicators.note: words in a mess are jumbled up, so these two little words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A palace functionary complains that his quarters were abandoned untidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a mess' reads as untidy, but 'mess' only scrambles the two small words before it; the possessive 's is a link meaning is.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lord Chamberlain is the senior officer running a royal household.

clue.text: Posts articles for paper

explanation.surface: Mail and pieces written for a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Columns are upright pillars like posts, and regular newspaper features written by columnists.

clue.text: 18 across's very Italian

parts.note: a word a player of music reads on a score in that language, meaning very, as in allegro ...

explanation.surface: A performer is said to be thoroughly Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Assai is the Italian tempo marking meaning very, used by performers of music.

clue.text: British taxi drivers' organisation keep one lot of odds and ends

indicators.note: the group of pieces keeps, or holds, the single letter inside them

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
the RAC, the Royal Automobile Club, is a British motoring organisation
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A British cab drivers' body hangs on to one heap of miscellaneous junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep' sets the numeral inside the pieces, just after the British abbreviation. The RAC is a British breakdown and motoring club for drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Bric-a-brac is a jumble of small ornaments and trinkets, miscellaneous oddments.

clue.text: Stagger in wind

explanation.surface: Someone lurches in a gale.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel is to sway or totter, and to reel in a fish line is to wind it.

clue.text: Read news strangely, but was satisfactory

indicators.note: strangely signals that these letters appear in an odd, rearranged order

explanation.surface: Someone reads the news in an odd voice yet the broadcast goes fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' turns READ NEWS into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that answered served its purpose or met the need, so it was adequate.

clue.text: Crane damaged by Pearl's mother, say

indicators.note: damaged signals that the letters of the bird are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A crane bird is injured by a pearl diver's mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges CRANE. 'Pearl's mother' is a cryptic way to say mother-of-pearl.
explanation.definitionFit: Nacre is the iridescent lining of shells, also called mother-of-pearl.

clue.text: Quick reply from letter I posted

indicators.note: from signals that the answer is taken out of the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: A swift response arrives to a letter I mailed.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick sharp retort, originally a fencer's return thrust.

clue.text: Go in to call on hard old tribesman

indicators.note: Go in tells us the word go sits inside another word

parts.note: to call on someone is to visit them
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An instruction to enter and pay a visit to a tough ancient tribal warrior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go in' reads as an instruction to enter, but it says the word go sits inside the verb for call on, before the T.
explanation.definitionFit: The Visigoths were a western branch of the Goths who sacked Rome in 410.

clue.text: Enlists us to work, having robust health

indicators.note: putting letters to work sets them moving into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A recruiting sergeant signs us up for labour, admiring our vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to work' rearranges ENLISTS US.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustiness is vigour and strength, a hearty physical condition.

clue.text: Firm making chip for Americans

explanation.surface: A company producing fried potato snacks for the US market.
explanation.definitionFit: Crisp means firm and brittle, and what Americans call a potato chip the British call a crisp.

clue.text: Girl goes to an open space in Bombay

parts.note: maid is an old word for a girl or young woman
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young woman heads for a park in Mumbai.
explanation.walkthrough: Bombay is the old name for Mumbai in India.
explanation.definitionFit: In India and Pakistan a maidan is an open public ground or esplanade.

clue.text: Not members of the Orthodox faith?

definitions.text: Not members of the Orthodox faith?

parts.words: Not members of the Orthodox faith?
parts.note: reads like Catholics or Protestants, outsiders to the Eastern church, but means people who reject orthodox belief

explanation.surface: A question about people outside the Eastern church.
explanation.definitionFit: Heretics hold opinions contrary to accepted doctrine, so they are not orthodox.

clue.text: Father received question from escort

indicators.note: one word receives, or takes in, another inside it

parts.note: a sire is a father, especially of an animal

explanation.surface: A dad took a question from his date's chaperone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father' suggests a priest, but here it is the word for a male parent of an animal; 'received' wraps it round the question abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To squire a lady is to accompany her as a gentleman attendant.

clue.text: Anonymous, such a letter given no notice?

definitions.text: such a letter given no notice?

explanation.surface: An anonymous note that nobody paid attention to.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the answer as UN-SIGNED: a letter with no sign, or notice, given to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter without a signature has no named author, and read playfully it has not been signalled.

clue.text: So here's a surprise at the coast

indicators.note: a surprise jolts things into an unexpected order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker exclaims in delight on reaching the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprise' rearranges SO HERES A; the 's is spelt out as an S here. 'at the' links.
explanation.definitionFit: The coast is the land along the sea, the shore by the water.

clue.text: Extra weight carried in car?

parts.note: suggests the additional wheel in a boot, and also a roll of fat round a person's waist

explanation.surface: A question about extra load in a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserve wheel kept in the boot, and slang for a ring of belly fat.

clue.text: Chewed odd pear I sent up

indicators.note: chewed food is mashed about, so these letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone recounts eating a strange pear and dispatching it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chewed' rearranges ODD PEAR I.
explanation.definitionFit: To send up is to mock by imitation, the same as making a spoof of something.

clue.text: He has to interpret notes from the staff

definitions.text: He has to interpret notes from the staff

parts.words: He has to interpret notes from the staff
parts.note: sounds like an office worker reading memos from employees, but the staff is the musical stave and notes are musical

explanation.surface: A manager must make sense of memos sent by employees.
explanation.definitionFit: A player reads music written on the stave and performs it.

clue.text: Sage's mother going round Panama, perhaps

indicators.note: one word goes round another, enclosing it

parts.note: mama is a word for mother
a Panama is a kind of straw hat, so perhaps flags an example

explanation.surface: A wise man's mum travels around a Central American country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' wraps mother around the hat. Panama looks like the country, but is the straw hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma, meaning great soul, is a title given to a revered wise person in India.

clue.text: Got ready for accountant to cast

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
to cast skin or leaves is to shed them

explanation.surface: Someone prepared for a bookkeeper to throw something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' is slang for cash (ready money), so 'got ready' means converted into money.
explanation.definitionFit: To cash a cheque is to obtain money for it, ready being slang for money.

clue.text: Curiously, not dead, but passed on

indicators.note: curiously signals the letters come out in a peculiar order

explanation.surface: Oddly, someone is said to have passed on yet isn't dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curiously' rearranges NOT DEAD. 'passed on' looks like died, but means handed over.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass something on to a charity is to give it away as a gift.

clue.text: Egghead's disbelieving expression?

explanation.surface: A clever person raises an eyebrow in doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the answer as HIGH BROW, an eyebrow raised in disbelief.
explanation.definitionFit: An intellectual is called a highbrow, and a lifted eyebrow shows scepticism.

clue.text: Tolerates wild animals

explanation.surface: Someone puts up with savage beasts.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something is to endure it, and grizzlies and pandas are large wild animals.

clue.text: Admiral's in the hold

explanation.surface: A naval commander is below deck in the cargo space.
explanation.walkthrough: The hold is a wrestling grip, not a ship's cargo space.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatio Nelson was the British admiral at Trafalgar, and a nelson is a wrestling neck lock.

clue.text: Clean stroke by batsman

explanation.surface: A tidy shot played by a cricketer.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a sweep is a shot played on one knee, swinging the bat across the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweep a floor is to brush it clean, and a sweep is a cricket batting shot.

clue.text: An account of back street deeds

indicators.note: back tells us the abbreviation for street is read from right to left

explanation.surface: A report of what happened in a back alley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back street' looks like an alley, but 'back' turns only the street abbreviation; 'An' and 'of' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Acts are things done, actions or achievements.

clue.text: Foreign character joins the army

parts.note: taken as written
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: An overseas oddball enlists as a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign character' is a letter of a foreign alphabet, here Greek, not an alien person.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Desire to travel, crawling some distance

parts.note: skin that is crawling feels itchy
feet are units for measuring distance

explanation.surface: A yearning to roam while creeping over a long way.
explanation.definitionFit: Having restless feet is an idiom for wanting to move on or wander.

clue.text: Avoided pits-speeded round

indicators.note: round signals the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A racing driver dodged trouble as the pit lane sped by on a lap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' rearranges PITS-SPEEDED.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidestep something is to dodge it by stepping aside.
